title: The tribunal process becomes operational
detail: Bangladesh activates the International Crimes Tribunal process under the 1973 law, moving 1971-related accountability from long-standing political demand into an active judicial framework.

title: The first ICT verdict signals the tribunal's practical reach
detail: The Abul Kalam Azad verdict showed that the tribunal had moved from institutional setup to concrete sentencing, making the justice process newly visible in public life.

title: The Quader Mollah verdict triggers Shahbag
detail: The ICT verdict in the Abdul Quader Mollah case was read by many activists as too lenient, and the reaction rapidly developed into the Shahbag movement's demand for stronger accountability.

title: Amendment and appeal battles intensify justice politics
detail: The tribunal era fed directly into legal amendment, appellate judgment, and expanding public argument over sentencing, due process, and the political uses of 1971 memory.
